title: Jude and the Crown Anew
premise: Petra Dunmore, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, a trade house that brokers miracles, curses, and memories for coin. When prayers to the old gods begin landing on her desk like deliveries, she discovers the gods are not returning — they are being smuggled back, one stolen name at a time, by someone inside her own guild. With Jude, a memoryless courier who may be the vessel of a forgotten god, Petra must decide whether to expose the smuggling and reignite an ancient war or protect the secret and let the old gods die quietly. In the end, Petra sacrifices her own oath-memories to give the gods a new, gentler crown: mortality shared among mortals, with Jude choosing love over divinity.
about_author: I. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing broken contracts and unclaimed inheritances before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, oaths, and the people who keep both from catching fire.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Miracles
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She audits the guild's winter ledgers and finds three entries for prayers answered in a city where the gods have been silent for four hundred years. The emotional beat is quiet unease beneath professional calm; she burns one page and immediately regrets it.

chapters.title: A Courier Without Yesterday
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The guild's best courier wakes with no memory beyond two years ago and a delivery satchel that hums when opened. Petra interviews them about a missing parcel. The beat is wary attraction: two people recognizing loneliness in each other's bookkeeping.

chapters.title: What the Satchel Sang
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The satchel contains a god's name, folded small enough to fit in a palm. When Petra reads it aloud by accident, every candle in the guildhall leans toward her. She realizes the smuggling is real, and that her swordspeaker oath can still hear it. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Guild of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A tour of the guild's vaults, brokers, and rules, interrupted when Master Vellam, Petra's mentor, asks too casually what she found in the winter ledgers. Beat: the reader learns the institution's charm while suspecting its rot.

chapters.title: Nine Names Missing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude is sent to collect a debt from a temple ruin and finds nine altars scraped clean, their god-names cut out like pages. Something followed them home. Beat: first brush with real danger, and Jude's reflexive, impossible skill with a blade they don't remember learning.

chapters.title: Oath-Bound, Oath-Broken
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra visits the grave of her order and confesses her discovery to a dead commander. Flashback establishes the swordspeaker oath: speak a true name, bind a true thing. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve; she decides to investigate rather than report.

chapters.title: The Broker of Rain
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Petra and Jude trace a smuggled name to a rain-broker who sells weather to drought towns. Under interrogation, he reveals names pass through a middleman called the Tithe. Beat: uneasy alliance cemented; first spark of trust between them.

chapters.title: Vellam's Kindness
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Vellam covers for Petra's unauthorized inquiry — too generously. She finds her own audit notes altered in his hand. Beat: betrayal as a slow cold realization rather than a shock; the mentor becomes the prime suspect.

chapters.title: The Road to the Tithe
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Travel chapter: Jude and Petra pose as husband-and-wife couriers on the salt road. Around a fire, Jude admits the terror of having no past; Petra offers to be their witness instead. Beat: love against duty begins here, tender and unsaid.

chapters.title: The Tithe
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The middleman is not a person but a shrine that eats one memory per transaction. To learn the buyer's identity, Petra pays with a memory of her commander's face. Beat: sacrifice establishing cost; the war's stakes become personal.

chapters.title: A Crown in Pieces
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The buyer is revealed: not Vellam alone but a cabal of guild founders reassembling the Crown Anew, the artifact that once forced all gods into servitude. Beat: horror at the scale; the secret could reignite the Godswar if either side learns of it.

chapters.title: What Jude Forgot
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The Tithe's payment echoes strangely: Jude recovers a fragment — they were the Crown's intended vessel, emptied and escaped. Beat: identity crisis; Jude wonders if their love for Petra was even theirs.

chapters.title: The Founders' Table
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Petra confronts the surviving founders at a banquet, playing for time while Jude steals the Crown's keystone page from the vault below. Beat: high-tension social chess; Vellam lets them go, and Petra finally understands why.

chapters.title: Vellam's Confession
chapters.summary: Vellam's POV (epistolary letter). He explains he emptied Jude to save them from being the Crown's slave-vessel, and has been smuggling god-names to hide them from the founders. Beat: moral inversion; the villain-suspect becomes a tragic guardian.

chapters.title: War Weather
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Omens gather: rivers running backward, soldiers dreaming in dead tongues. Both the church and the old gods' remnants sense the Crown moving. Beat: ticking clock made literal; time is running out.

chapters.title: The Choice at Greyford Bridge
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Cornered by founders' enforcers, Jude can restore their full memory — and become the vessel again — or stay half-made and lose the fight. They choose to remember. Beat: devastating power unleashed, and grief for the self they were becoming.

chapters.title: Swordspeech
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra speaks her first true name in fifteen years to hold the bridge, binding herself to the Crown's keystone so no one else can carry it. Beat: triumph laced with doom; the oath will consume her memories as long as she holds it.

chapters.title: The Gods Answer
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The freed god-names arrive at the guildhall, not as conquerors but as petitioners, asking what mortals intend for them. Beat: awe and terror; the ancient war teeters on a single conversation.

chapters.title: The Negotiation of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Through one endless night, Petra bargains: the gods accept mortality distributed among willing bearers instead of a crown or a war. Beat: exhausted, human diplomacy winning where armies couldn't; love declared openly between Petra and Jude amid the candle-glow.

chapters.title: The Founders' Reckoning
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The founders attempt to seize the keystone anyway; Vellam dies holding the door, and the guild votes itself out of the miracle trade. Beat: cathartic climax resolution; the price paid is counted honestly.

chapters.title: What Petra Gave
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The oath releases its price: Petra loses her memories of the order, the bridge, and nearly Jude. Jude, keeper of their own recovered past, becomes hers. Beat: bittersweet tenderness; love against duty resolved into love as duty freely chosen.

chapters.title: Jude and the Crown Anew
chapters.summary: Dual POV, epilogue. A year later, the guild trades only possible things. Jude carries a small crown of mortal names; Petra writes a new ledger whose first entry is a promise. Beat: quiet hope — the secret kept, the war unfought, the future unwritten and theirs.
